subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Tagore, Raman, Sen, Satyarthi, Khorana, and Ramakrishnan.

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian citizen (and first Asian) to win a Nobel Prize?

options.option_text: Rabindranath Tagore
C. V. Raman
Mother Teresa
Hargobind Khorana

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian, and the first Asian, to win a Nobel Prize. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. The prize was awarded "because of his profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse," largely recognizing his self-translated English collection 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings), which had a profound impact on Western literary circles (championed by W.B. Yeats).
DECOY BUSTING: Sir C.V. Raman was the first Indian scientist to win (Physics, 1930). Mother Teresa won the Peace Prize in 1979. Hargobind Khorana (an Indian-American) won for Medicine in 1968.
EXAM INSIGHT: Tagore's win shattered the Eurocentric bias of the Nobel Prize. He used the prize money to fund his experimental school at Santiniketan, which later grew into the Visva-Bharati University.

questions.stem: Sir C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his work on:

options.option_text: The scattering of light and the discovery of the Raman Effect
The mathematical formulation of the Chandrasekhar Limit for black holes
The development of the Bose-Einstein statistics
The discovery of the structure of DNA

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics "for his work on the scattering of light and for the discovery of the effect named after him." The Raman Effect occurs when light traverses a transparent material, and some of the deflected light changes wavelength and amplitude. This phenomenon revolutionized molecular spectroscopy.
DECOY BUSTING: The Chandrasekhar Limit was discovered by Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (Raman's nephew, who won the Nobel in 1983). Bose-Einstein statistics were developed by Satyendra Nath Bose (who famously never received a Nobel). DNA structure was Watson, Crick, and Franklin.
EXAM INSIGHT: Raman made his discovery on February 28, 1928, using extremely simple, locally made equipment in Calcutta. In his honor, February 28 is celebrated annually in India as National Science Day.

questions.stem: Amartya Sen, the first Asian to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences (1998), was recognized primarily for his contributions to:

options.option_text: Welfare economics, specifically his research on the causes of famines and poverty
Game theory and the Nash Equilibrium
Behavioral economics and the concept of 'nudge'
Macroeconomic growth theory and the Solow model

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Amartya Sen was awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economics "for his contributions to welfare economics." His most groundbreaking work demonstrated that famines do not occur merely from a lack of food supply (crop failure), but from inequalities built into the mechanisms for distributing food (lack of "entitlements" or purchasing power). He famously argued that no substantial famine has ever occurred in a functioning democracy with a free press.
DECOY BUSTING: Game theory is associated with John Nash. Behavioral economics/nudge is Richard Thaler. Growth theory is Robert Solow.
EXAM INSIGHT: Sen's capability approach heavily influenced the creation of the United Nations Human Development Index (HDI), developed alongside his colleague Mahbub ul Haq. Sen was also awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

questions.stem: Which Indian child rights activist shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 with Pakistan's Malala Yousafzai?

options.option_text: Kailash Satyarthi
Medha Patkar
Bindeshwar Pathak
Sundarlal Bahuguna

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Kailash Satyarthi was jointly awarded the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai "for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education." Satyarthi founded the 'Bachpan Bachao Andolan' (Save the Childhood Movement) in 1980, which has rescued tens of thousands of children from hazardous industries, bonded labor, and trafficking in India.
DECOY BUSTING: Medha Patkar is the face of the Narmada Bachao Andolan. Bindeshwar Pathak founded Sulabh International (sanitation). Sundarlal Bahuguna was a leader of the Chipko movement.
EXAM INSIGHT: The joint award to an older Indian Hindu man and a young Pakistani Muslim girl was seen as a powerful statement by the Nobel Committee, emphasizing that the fight for children's education and rights transcends borders and religions.

questions.stem: Har Gobind Khorana, an Indian-born American biochemist, shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work demonstrating how:

options.option_text: The order of nucleotides in nucleic acids controls the cell's synthesis of proteins (cracking the genetic code)
Penicillin acts as an antibiotic to destroy bacterial cell walls
Malaria parasites are transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito
Blood groups are classified into the ABO system

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Har Gobind Khorana (born in undivided India, later a US citizen) shared the 1968 Nobel Prize with Robert Holley and Marshall Nirenberg. They essentially "cracked the genetic code." Khorana's experiments showed exactly how the specific sequence of nucleotides in DNA and RNA dictates the sequence of amino acids built into proteins. He was also the first scientist to chemically synthesize an artificial gene in a laboratory.
DECOY BUSTING: Penicillin's mechanism was Fleming, Florey, and Chain. Malaria transmission was Ronald Ross (born in India, won Nobel in 1902). ABO blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner.
EXAM INSIGHT: Khorana's work bridged the gap between genetics and biochemistry. His ability to synthesize oligonucleotides laid the technological groundwork for modern biotechnology, including the development of PCR and genetic engineering.

questions.stem: Venkatraman 'Venki' Ramakrishnan, an Indian-born structural biologist, won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his studies on the structure and function of which cellular organelle?

options.option_text: Ribosome
Mitochondrion
Nucleus
Golgi Apparatus

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Venki Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Thomas A. Steitz and Ada E. Yonath. They used X-ray crystallography to map the structure of the ribosome down to the atomic level. The ribosome is the cell's protein factory, translating DNA information into functional proteins. 
DECOY BUSTING: He did not work on mitochondria (the powerhouse), the nucleus (the control center), or the Golgi apparatus (the packaging center). 
EXAM INSIGHT: Understanding the precise 3D structure of the bacterial ribosome has massive medical applications. Because many antibiotics (like tetracycline and streptomycin) work by binding to bacterial ribosomes and paralyzing them, Ramakrishnan's structural maps have allowed pharmaceutical companies to design newer, more effective antibiotics to combat drug-resistant bacteria.

questions.stem: In which year did Mother Teresa, who dedicated her life to serving the destitute in Kolkata, receive the Nobel Peace Prize?

options.option_text: 1975 (International Women's Year declared by the UN)
1979 (year the Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan)
1983 (year Chandrasekhar won the Nobel Physics Prize)
1986 (year of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in USSR)

questions.explanation: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her work caring for the sick and poor through the Missionaries of Charity. 1983 is a common confusion because Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar won the Physics Nobel that year, making it a memorable year for Indian Nobel laureates.

questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore was awarded the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature primarily for which work?

options.option_text: Gora, a novel exploring Hindu-Christian social tensions
Gitanjali (Song Offerings), a collection of devotional verses
Manasi, his early anthology on romantic and lyrical themes
Chokher Bali, a prose work on women and social conditions

questions.explanation: The Swedish Academy specifically cited Gitanjali (Song Offerings) — Tagore's own English prose-poetry translation — for its 'profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse.' Gora and Chokher Bali are well-known Tagore novels but were not the basis of the award.

questions.stem: The 'Chandrasekhar Limit' of approximately 1.4 solar masses, for which Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics, defines the:

options.option_text: Maximum mass a white dwarf star can have without collapsing
Minimum core temperature needed to initiate hydrogen fusion in a star
Critical radius at which a neutron star collapses into a black hole
Maximum luminosity a star can sustain before shedding mass via radiation

questions.explanation: The Chandrasekhar Limit (~1.4 M☉) is the upper mass boundary for a stable white dwarf; above this, electron degeneracy pressure cannot halt gravitational collapse. Option C describes the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff limit, which applies to neutron stars — a separate concept often confused with Chandrasekhar's work.

questions.stem: Mother Teresa established the Missionaries of Charity in 1950 to serve the sick and dying poor. In which city was this congregation formally founded?

options.option_text: New Delhi, near the central government's charitable institutions
Mumbai, in the densely populated Dharavi slum settlement area
Kolkata (then Calcutta), where she had been working since 1929
Chennai, the port city she first entered when coming to India

questions.explanation: Teresa arrived in India in 1929 at Loreto Convent, Darjeeling, then moved to Kolkata. She received permission to leave the Loreto order and founded Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata on 7 October 1950. Mumbai and Delhi are common wrong guesses due to their prominence in social-welfare discourse.

questions.stem: Amartya Sen's 1981 study 'Poverty and Famines,' central to his 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, concluded that historical famines (including Bengal 1943) were primarily caused by:

options.option_text: Absolute food shortage triggered by droughts and widespread crop failures
Collapse of food entitlements rather than any actual decline in food supply
Overpopulation outpacing agricultural output in the affected regions
Colonial export policies forcibly diverting food to European markets

questions.explanation: Sen's 'entitlement approach' showed that in Bengal 1943, food availability actually rose — the famine was caused by a breakdown in people's entitlements (purchasing power, access rights). Option D is a popular nationalist narrative but Sen's empirical analysis shows supply was not the binding constraint.

questions.stem: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 while working at which research institution in Kolkata?

options.option_text: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata
Bose Institute, founded by Jagadish Chandra Bose in north Kolkata
University Science College under Calcutta University's physics wing
Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, established by Meghnad Saha

questions.explanation: Raman made the discovery at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), where he served as Palit Professor. The Bose Institute and Saha Institute are common distractors — both were founded by celebrated Indian scientists in Kolkata, but Raman's Nobel-linked work was rooted at IACS. 28 February is now observed as National Science Day.

questions.stem: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize with Robert Holley and Marshall Nirenberg. While Nirenberg first decoded a codon using cell-free translation, Khorana's distinctive technical contribution was:

options.option_text: Chemically synthesizing defined polynucleotide sequences to verify codon assignments
Discovering that the genetic code is a non-overlapping triplet read without punctuation
Identifying the ribosome as the organelle where protein synthesis physically occurs
Demonstrating that multiple codons can encode the same amino acid (degeneracy)

questions.explanation: Khorana pioneered the chemical synthesis of oligonucleotides with defined sequences, enabling systematic experimental confirmation of the complete codon table. Option B describes a conceptual framework proposed earlier by Francis Crick's group; option C refers to general cell biology established by multiple researchers. Khorana later (1970) also achieved the first total synthesis of an artificial gene, building on this Nobel-winning chemical methodology.
